- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.5) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, cap the peak at 10–15% above recent high to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.3) and forecast is persistently high, apply downward bias of 3–5% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline after a peak, adjust forecast to reflect 2–3 day lag in price correction.  
- If sentiment history shows recent volatility (e.g., alternating 0.00 and 0.50), reduce forecast variance by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noisy sentiment signals.
